findings.title: Editable levels and reversible parameters permit forged leaderboard scores
findings.entry_point: A local cheater supplies a user-edited .defence file through the menu Load action (ApoDefenceOptions.java:170-172), replaces the automatically loaded user.dir/levels/Original_First.defence file (ApoDefenceGame.java:176), or recreates the public submission protocol exposed by ApoDefenceHighscore.send() (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:166-203).
findings.sink: A GET request containing the client-supplied map, level and points is issued to highscore.php when getInputStream() is called (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:191-203).
findings.data_path: Load -> ApoDefenceGame.setLoad() -> ApoDefenceLoadSave.readLevel() (ApoDefenceGame.java:347-368). readLevel derives the leaderboard map solely from the selected filename and imports money, wave and enemy values (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:154,185-195). The original-settings gate compares money, tower and wave values against that same loaded file (ApoDefenceOptionsGeneral.java:156-164; ApoDefenceOptions.java:81-88). After a win/loss, Upload calls highscore.send() (ApoDefenceGame.java:395-432,772-778), which applies only repeated Base64 and a Base64-encoded day-of-month before sending the query (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:166-203; ApoDefenceHighscoreEncrypt.java:3-8,61-63).
findings.attack_scenario: Create an easy level named Original_First.defence with excessive starting money, weak enemy ordering and otherwise default tuning. Load it and finish the altered map. Because its basename is treated as the map identity and its own values satisfy the local original check, the client offers Upload for the Original_First leaderboard. A cheater can also generate a request directly, replacing points with five rounds of standard Base64 and cor with two rounds of Base64 over the current day. If the endpoint trusts this documented client protocol, the attacker gains a fraudulent leaderboard entry.
findings.preconditions: The historical high-score service or a compatible replacement must be reachable, canConnect() must succeed, and the server must not perform additional authoritative game validation absent from this source. Loading the altered level requires write access to the default levels directory or user selection through the chooser.
findings.validation_plan: Against an authorized staging instance, create a valid easy .defence file named Original_First.defence, leave the option tunings at defaults, load and finish it, and capture the Upload GET through an HTTP proxy. Decode name three times, map four times, level twice and points five times with standard Base64; confirm that the request claims map Original_First despite altered level contents. Then, using a disposable nickname, replay the request with points encoding 999999 and a correctly encoded current day. Retrieval of that value in highscore.xml proves server-side exploitability.

findings.title: High-score retrieval and submission use unauthenticated HTTP
findings.entry_point: On a win or loss, ApoDefenceGame.think() invokes the high-score client (ApoDefenceGame.java:395-405,422-432), causing network traffic to fixed HTTP URLs.
findings.sink: ImageIO.read(URL), URL.openStream() and HttpURLConnection.getInputStream() exchange the connectivity probe, high-score XML and score submission without TLS (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:61-64,81-87,191-203).
findings.data_path: ApoDefenceTimer.run() -> ApoDefenceGame.think() -> ApoDefenceHighscore.canConnect()/makeEntity() for reads (ApoDefenceTimer.java:42-48; ApoDefenceGame.java:395-405,422-432), and the Upload mouse action -> ApoDefenceHighscore.send() for writes (ApoDefenceGame.java:772-778; ApoDefenceHighscore.java:166-203).
findings.attack_scenario: A network attacker intercepts HTTP for home.arcor.de and daporius.drition.net, returns a valid probe image, then alters highscore.xml to display fabricated rankings. When the player clicks Upload, the attacker reads the nickname and score and changes the points or map query before forwarding it. This compromises leaderboard integrity and can selectively suppress the online feature.
findings.preconditions: The player reaches a win/loss screen and the attacker controls DNS, a proxy, Wi-Fi, or another network hop. The original domains need not be honest or currently live if the attacker can redirect their plain-HTTP names.
findings.validation_plan: Route both fixed hosts through a controlled HTTP proxy or DNS override. Return a valid small GIF for test.gif, serve well-formed highscore.xml with a distinctive fabricated nickname, and verify that the game renders it. Capture an Upload request, modify its points parameter in transit, and verify at the controlled receiver that the modified plaintext request arrives. A packet capture should show that neither direction is encrypted or authenticated.

findings.title: Eight-byte level header can drive multi-gigabyte image allocation
findings.entry_point: An editable default level is loaded automatically from user.dir/levels/Original_First.defence (ApoDefenceGame.java:176), and arbitrary local .defence files can also be selected through the Load chooser (ApoDefenceOptions.java:170-172; ApoDefenceGame.java:347-362).
findings.sink: Unvalidated dimensions control new int[y][x] in readLevel() (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:156-164) and subsequently new BufferedImage(x*32, y*32, TYPE_INT_RGB) (ApoDefenceGame.java:210-225).
findings.data_path: The file chooser or automatic startup path reaches ApoDefenceLoadSave.readLevel(). It reads two signed integers without bounds or overflow checks and allocates the grid (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:145-164). If the file ends there, EOFException is logged but no failure is returned or state rolled back (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:198-208). ApoDefenceGame.setLoad() nevertheless calls restart() (ApoDefenceGame.java:362-368), which propagates x/y and invokes makeNewXAndY() (ApoDefenceGame.java:1048-1096), multiplying each dimension by 32 for a second allocation.
findings.attack_scenario: Place or distribute an eight-byte .defence file containing big-endian integers 1000 and 1000. The first allocation is roughly 4 MB, after which EOF is swallowed. The caller continues with the partial state and attempts a 32000-by-32000 RGB image, requiring roughly 4 GB of pixel storage. On an ordinary game JVM this causes OutOfMemoryError or termination. Replacing the predictable default level can trigger the crash at startup; otherwise the victim must select the file.
findings.preconditions: The attacker can modify the default level file or persuade the user to open a malicious/user-generated .defence file. The JVM heap is smaller than the attacker-selected allocation, as is normal for the example dimensions.
findings.validation_plan: Create oom.defence using DataOutputStream.writeInt(1000) twice and no further bytes. Run the game with -Xmx256m and either replace levels/Original_First.defence or select oom.defence using Load. Confirmation is an EOFException message followed by an uncaught OutOfMemoryError or allocation failure whose stack includes ApoDefenceGame.makeNewXAndY()/BufferedImage. Repeat with 20-by-15 dimensions as a control; it should not exhaust memory.

findings.title: Unbounded synchronous high-score reads can hang or exhaust the game
findings.entry_point: A malicious high-score server or network interceptor controls the response body returned from the fixed test.gif and highscore.xml HTTP URLs (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:61-64,81-87).
findings.sink: ImageIO.read(URL) and URL.openStream() have no configured connect/read timeout, while Scanner.next() searches for end-of-input and materializes the complete XML response as one String (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:61-75,78-87).
findings.data_path: ApoDefenceTimer.run() synchronously calls ApoDefenceGame.think() (ApoDefenceTimer.java:42-48). The win/loss branches synchronously call canConnect() and makeEntity() on that timer thread (ApoDefenceGame.java:395-405,422-432). Those methods perform blocking reads and whole-response buffering before returning (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:61-87).
findings.attack_scenario: When the player wins or loses, the attacker accepts the test.gif connection and never completes its response, indefinitely blocking the timer task. Alternatively, the attacker supplies a valid probe GIF and an endless or very large highscore.xml body; Scanner waits for EOF while retaining the token, growing the heap until the game stalls or throws OutOfMemoryError.
findings.preconditions: The player reaches a win/loss state and the malicious server, DNS responder, proxy or network attacker can answer the HTTP request. The large-XML branch also requires the local original-settings check to pass; stalling the initial probe does not.
findings.validation_plan: Redirect the fixed hosts to a controlled HTTP server. First accept the test.gif request but never send EOF; use jstack to confirm ApoDefenceTimer is blocked below ImageIO/URLConnection and observe that game updates cease. In a second run, return a valid GIF and stream highscore.xml indefinitely or to a size exceeding a constrained -Xmx256m heap. Increasing heap usage followed by OutOfMemoryError at Scanner.next()/makeEntity confirms the unbounded-read path.

notes: The source root contains only 67 Java files; no resources, packaged levels, build metadata or high-score server implementation were supplied. Consequently, current availability of the historical domains and any unseen server-side score validation were not tested. Project-wide API/import searches found no ClassLoader/defineClass path, ObjectInputStream/readObject, MessageDigest, JNI/System.load, applet, process execution or credential literal. No shared-level download client exists in this variant: .defence exposure is through the automatic user.dir load and local file choosers.
